# The Origin Engine API

`@origingame/engine`, API version 1: 41 modules, generated from `crates/og-api/api.ogt`. Each module has an overview page and every function, component and type a page of its own under `<module>/`; every signature is quoted from the IDL. `og api find <words>` ranks every entry; `og api show <name>` prints one.

The Origin Engine API. Game code declares components and systems, and reads the world through typed views over engine memory.

Every failure is a returned Result; desc objects may omit any field; nothing reads the wall clock inside a tick.

## Modules

| Module | TypeScript | Publish builds | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`math`](math.md) | types and tokens | kept | Plain math values in the three.js vocabulary. They are data: the engine owns the operations, so results are identical on every host. |
| [`reflect`](reflect.md) | named exports | kept | Reflection: components and resources are declared once with their field layout and metadata, and registered by name. |
| [`world`](world.md) | types and tokens | kept | The world: an archetype ECS. Entities are generational handles; components are columns in engine memory. |
| [`system`](system.md) | named exports | kept | Systems: functions the engine calls once per tick with their matched archetypes. |
| [`game`](game.md) | `og.*` | kept | The game entry: what the bundle's default export declares. |
| [`transform`](transform.md) | `og.transform.*` | kept | Transforms in the three.js vocabulary: position, quaternion and scale, composed into matrixWorld down the parent chain. |
| [`time`](time.md) | `og.time.*` | kept | Simulation time. Game code never reads the wall clock; it reads Time. |
| [`rng`](rng.md) | types and tokens | kept | Deterministic randomness. Every random draw comes from an Rng stream; the sequence for a seed is identical on every host and in the Web scaffold's rng.ts. |
| [`procgen`](procgen.md) | `og.procgen.*` | kept | Procedural generation: gradient noise (Perlin, simplex, FBM), Poisson-disk points, BSP dungeons and wave function collapse, all deterministic. Each generator takes a `seed`; give it the seed of a fork of og.Rng, `world.resource(og.Rng)`'s value `.fork("dungeon").seed` (a fork needs og.Rng among a system's reads only), so the same world and label give the same output and the main stream does not move. A generator draws only from a stream on that seed, in a fixed order, with arithmetic that is bit-identical on every host: the same seed gives the same map natively and on the web, in a replay and after a restore. |
| [`input`](input.md) | `og.input.*` | kept | Input as the game sees it: the Input resource for polling, events for edges. |
| [`camera`](camera.md) | `og.camera.*` | kept | The main camera, as a resource with three.js PerspectiveCamera and OrthographicCamera parameter names. |
| [`render`](render.md) | `og.render.*` | kept | What is drawn: meshes with materials. Draws are instanced by (geometry, material) automatically; there is no per-object draw call. |
| [`shapes`](shapes.md) | types and tokens | kept | Two-dimensional outlines in three.js's words: og.Shape and og.Path2 are three.js's Shape and Path, built by the same calls (moveTo, lineTo, quadraticCurveTo, bezierCurveTo, splineThru, arc, absarc, ellipse, absellipse, closePath) and flattened to points by getPoints, so a three.js outline is a paste. og.render.shapeGeometry, extrudeGeometry and sweepGeometry take them; only their points cross to the engine. |
| [`load`](load.md) | `og.load.*` | kept | Asset loading from cooked output: `og cook` turns assets/ into cooked/ (.ogb blobs and the manifest cooked/.cook.ogt), and the runtime reads only cooked/. |
| [`physics`](physics.md) | `og.physics.*` | kept | Rigid bodies over rapier (rapier3d in the 3D profile, rapier2d in 2D, both with enhanced determinism): game code owns the components, the engine's og.physics system steps them after the game's systems and writes the dynamic bodies back. |
| [`atmosphere`](atmosphere.md) | `og.atmosphere.*` | kept | Fog, a procedural sky, the day-night cycle, weather, the wind that sways vegetation and water, declared as resources and components (the E5 round). Everything is off by default: a world that sets none of them draws exactly as before. |
| [`anim`](anim.md) | `og.anim.*` | kept | Skeletal animation over og-anim: glTF skins and clips (cooked into the `<model>#anim` blob, loaded with og.load.animation), blend-tree graphs with layered state machines, root motion, two-bone and FABRIK IK and blendshapes, evaluated by the engine's og.anim system after the game's systems and before physics. |
| [`tween`](tween.md) | `og.tween.*` | kept | Tweens: animate any numeric field of a component (og.Transform.position, og.Sprite.color, og.Sprite.opacity, a game's own f32) from its value to a target over time with an easing curve, a delay, loops and yoyo; chain them in sequences or run them in parallel. Advanced by the engine's og.tween system after the game's systems and before og.anim and physics, by scaled time (slow motion, hit stop) unless unscaled. |
| [`tilemap`](tilemap.md) | `og.tilemap.*` | kept | Tilemaps: layers of tiles from a tileset atlas (an `.ogt` of `type tileset`: grid, solid tiles and collision rects, animated tiles, 47-blob and 16-bitmask auto-tiling terrains), loaded from a cooked map (a hand-written `.ogt` of `type tilemap`, a Tiled `.tmj` or an LDtk `.ldtk`) with og.load.tilemap and placed by an og.Tilemap component. |
| [`audio`](audio.md) | `og.audio.*` | kept | Sound: inside the tick, the engine's og.audio system (after the game's systems and physics) turns AudioSource changes into a deterministic, time-stamped command stream; outside the tick the host's mixer renders it (an AudioWorklet on the web, the output device, a capture or a null sink natively). |
| [`nav`](nav.md) | `og.nav.*` | kept | Navigation: grids (A* and jump point search with eight-way moves that never cut a blocked corner, line-of-sight smoothing), flow fields for crowds, and navmeshes (baked at cook time from a level's static colliders and models, or built at runtime for a flat procedural level) with funnel paths and box obstacles that rebuild only the tiles they touch. |
| [`ai`](ai.md) | `og.ai.*` | kept | Enemy and NPC AI as data: behaviour trees and state machines in `.ogt` files of `type behaviour`, perception (sight cones checked against physics occlusion, hearing of spatial sounds and game noises) and a blackboard per agent. |
| [`story`](story.md) | `og.story.*` | kept | Dialogue and quests as data: dialogues in `.ogt` files of `type dialogue` (speakers, nodes of lines, choices with conditions, reasons and checks, variables, weighted picks, timers) and quests in `type quest` files (stages of objectives, rewards, conditions), validated by og cook, which names each mistake's line and the fix. Text is never inline: every line, choice, reason, name and title is an og.i18n key, and og.story resolves it in the active locale when it is read, so a locale switch re-translates the line on screen. |
| [`platform`](platform.md) | `og.platform.*` | kept | Platform services as host capabilities (docs/design.md §2.8): cloud store, leaderboards, telemetry, Origin Point and AI marks. Game code names a method and its arguments, never a credential, a URL or a cookie: the host owns them. On the web the shell forwards each call to the Player through origin-checked postMessage (Player protocol 2, docs/web-export.md); natively the host answers from a local JSON store (`og run --platform-store`, default `<project>/.og/platform.json`). |
| [`i18n`](i18n.md) | `og.i18n.*` | kept | Localization: one string table per locale (`.ogt` of `type strings`: `locale "ja"`, its font chain `fonts "..."`, `string "key" "message"`), messages in a subset of ICU MessageFormat (`{name}`, `{n, number}`, `{n, plural, =0 {..} one {..} other {..}}` with `#`, `{g, select, a {..} other {..}}`), CLDR plural rules, and the locale the host asks for (the browser's `navigator.language` on the web, `og run --locale` natively). |
| [`ui`](ui.md) | `og.ui.*` | kept | The engine's UI: an immediate-mode toolkit. Systems describe the tree every tick with these calls; the engine lays it out Clay-style, styles it with the game's UI style (the engine's default style until the game picks one), draws it over the frame and answers the probe (dump_ui, touch_move_to, move_to_text) from it. |
| [`systems`](systems.md) | types and tokens | kept | Systems the engine ships as TypeScript: game-level code, listed explicitly in GameDesc.systems like the game's own, so the schedule (and dump_world) shows them and nothing runs that the game did not ask for. |
| [`commands`](commands.md) | `og.commands.*` | dropped | The command channel: actions scheduled on simulation time, from `og run --commands "t:action[:args];..."` or the probe's commands(). |
| [`probe`](probe.md) | types and tokens | kept | The probe: RuntimeProbe protocol 5 (origin/packages/contracts/src/probe.ts) served natively, plus the engine's wire members. |
| [`terrain`](terrain.md) | `og.terrain.*` | kept | Terrain (phase 2): a height field over a rectangle, cooked by `og cook` from a `type terrain` .ogt (a 16-bit grey PNG or an EXR heightmap, an optional control map, up to sixteen layered materials with slope and altitude rules (each pixel blends its four strongest), their maps separate textures (the first four layers) or layers of two texture arrays: `layers` and `layerNormals` with each layer's `albedoLayer` and `normalLayer`, two sampled textures instead of up to eight and the only way past four layers, the control map one image per four layers, and an optional `holes` map whose black or transparent cells are cut out of the surface: a cave mouth, a pit, a tunnel through a hill) into tiles; drawn as a geometry clipmap around the camera (nested levels by distance, no cracks) that casts and receives shadows under the fog; collided with as a height field; baked into navmeshes by a navmesh file's `terrain` entry. |
| [`stream`](stream.md) | `og.stream.*` | kept | Asset streaming groups (phase 3): a scene's `stream "<name>" { asset ...; distance x y z r [unload d] \| volume "<entity>"; priority n }` blocks name glTF models (without skins or morph targets), textures, texture arrays, flipbooks (an `array true` sheet brings its array), sounds, environment maps, palettes, looks and colour LUTs (`.cube`) that load and unload together, and what loads them: the camera within `r` of the anchor (kept until it is past `unload`, 1.25 r by default), the camera inside the named entity's box (its position ± half its scale, turned with it), or neither (og.stream.request only). `og cook` packs each group's files into `cooked/stream/<name>.ogb`; `og build --publish` ships the packs beside the boot bundle, which the shell and the service worker fetch first, and fetches a pack only when its group loads. |
| [`video`](video.md) | `og.video.*` | kept | Footage in a game (docs/design.md §2.9): a `type video` asset cooked by ffmpeg, loaded with og.load.video and played by og.VideoPlayer. A clip (the default, for short loops: at most 256 frames) is cooked into a texture array of its frames; a stream (`stream true`: any length) is cooked to AV1 and decoded as it plays, natively by rav1d on a thread of its own, on the web by WebCodecs, or by rav1d in a Worker of its own where the browser has no AV1 decoder (og.video.capabilities says which). Either way the frame shown is a Texture (VideoInfo.texture, also VideoPlayer.texture) any material map, og.Sprite or UI image draws, and the sound plays on the entity's og.AudioSource in step with it. |
| [`debug`](debug.md) | `og.debug.*` | dropped | Debug draw: lines, boxes, spheres, arrows, axes and labels in the world, each for a number of ticks, drawn over the finished frame (after every post effect, before the UI) so they read in every capture and never hide behind geometry; and the debug views (physics, navigation, bounds, levels of detail, and the lit image's terms: shadow cascades, ambient occlusion, albedo, image-based and direct light) the command channel's `debug:` actions switch. |
| [`assert`](assert.md) | `og.assert.*` | dropped | Assertions: properties of the game checked as it runs, after the Antithesis SDK's. `og.assert.always(world.get(hero, Health).hp >= 0, "hp never negative", { hp })` holds on every call, `og.assert.sometimes(boss.phase === 2, "boss reaches phase 2")` must hold at least once in a run, `og.assert.reachable("door opened")` must run at least once, `og.assert.unreachable("fell through the floor")` must never run, and `og.assert.each(level, cleared, "each level cleared")` keeps one bucket per distinct key, each of which must hold once. |
| [`path`](path.md) | `og.path.*` | kept | Paths: a curve through or controlled by points, measured by arc length so a parameter t from 0 to 1 moves along it at an even speed however its points are spaced. catmullRom passes through every point (three.js CatmullRomCurve3, tension 0.5), bezier chains cubic segments `p0 c0 c1 p1 c2 c3 p2 ...` (three.js CubicBezierCurve3 in a CurvePath), linear joins the points with straight segments. A closed path joins its last point to its first and wraps t. |
| [`timeline`](timeline.md) | `og.timeline.*` | kept | Timelines: cutscenes and sequences as data, Unity's Timeline and Godot's AnimationPlayer as an `.ogt` the agent reads and diffs. A `type timeline` file has a `duration` in seconds, `path "<name>" { ... }` blocks (as og.path's) and `track <kind> ["<entity>"] { key <seconds> { ... } }` blocks; `og cook` cooks it (importing caption files) and og.load.timeline loads it. Tracks: `camera` (position and target keys, or `rail "<path>"` with `at` 0..1 along it, or `follow "<entity>"` with offsets; fov; eased), `transform "<entity>"` (position, rotation in degrees or quaternion, scale; eased), `animation "<entity>"` (clip, speed, blendIn, loop; `model` names the glTF whose clips they are, else the entity's og.Model), `audio` (sound, volume, pitch, bus), `music` (sound, volume, fadeIn, fadeOut, end, loop, bus), `caption` (text from `key` to `end` with a UI type step `style` and an `anchor`; `captions "narration.srt" [offset]` imports a SubRip file or word timestamps `.json`), `event` (`do "<command-channel action>"`: teleport, set, a game's registered command; `retroactive true` runs it when a seek passes it), `transition` (kind cut, fade, wipe, dissolve, iris or slide; mode through, in or out; duration, color, from, over og.ui's screen cover) `marker` (`name`, sending og.TimelineMarker when played past), `property ["<entity>"]` (`field "og.PointLight.distance"`, keys of `value`: any reflected field of a component on the entity, or of a resource without one), `light "<entity>"` (its og.DirectionalLight, og.PointLight, og.SpotLight, og.RectLight or og.Light2D: color, intensity, distance, angle, ...), `visibility "<entity>"` (`visible true\|false` of whatever it draws, stepped), `post` (og.PostEffects' fields), `blendshape "<entity>"` (og.Blendshapes w0 to w7; its source becomes component), `material "<entity>"` (its og.Mesh's material, or its og.Model's material `index N`: StandardMaterialDesc fields by name, other names the material shader's parameters) and `timeline` (`play "<timeline>"`, speed, loop: from its key until the next, another timeline plays nested at (time − key) × speed, its markers sent as `<file>/<marker>`, at most four deep) and `shot` (`camera "<entity>"`, a virtual camera's name, or `none`; `blend` seconds and `ease`: from its key until the next, that og.VirtualCamera is og.CameraBrain.solo, blended to over the key's blend by its ease or by the camera's own; `none` and the timeline's end hand back the solo it found). Camera keys also take `roll` (degrees about the view direction), `focus` (a distance) or `focusOn "<entity>"` and `focusRange`, which set og.PostEffects' depth of field while the track owns the camera. The cook checks every field against the engine's records (a field the record lacks, one a timeline cannot drive, a value of the wrong shape) and refuses nesting in a cycle or deeper than four; a track kind this engine does not read is refused naming it and the engine's version. |
| [`net`](net.md) | `og.net.*` | kept | Deterministic lockstep over a room (docs/design.md §2.10): every peer runs the whole world, and what crosses the room is each player's input, one per tick, and the world's hash. Turn it on with og.Lockstep (`enabled`, `players`); join a room (og.platform.roomJoin, or `og run --room ws://127.0.0.1:P/<room>` with `og relay` natively). Until the room holds `players` peers the world runs freely on each (a lobby, the local input driving the local player); then the authority (the lowest peer number) starts: every other peer takes its world's snapshot, the seats go to the peers in number order, and from then on tick t runs only when every seated player's input for t is in. Once the room is full, the other peers' worlds hold for that snapshot (for at most stallTimeout, 5 s when it is 0), so a slow authority's start does not find them far into a lobby it replaces. A peer that joins a running room takes a free seat (or watches) from a snapshot a running peer hands it. |
| [`art`](art.md) | types and tokens | kept | A game's art contract: what every asset of its style holds, as seven resources a look sets beside the render ones (docs/art.md §2.1): the palette its texels sit on (ArtPalette), one pixel size for 2D art (ArtPixels), one texel density for 3D surfaces (ArtTexels), the shape language of its models (ArtShape), its line (ArtLine), the step of its motion (ArtMotion) and its camera (ArtCamera). A style is the assets, not a filter on the frame: the look's render resources treat the frame, these say what the assets themselves must be. |
| [`motion`](motion.md) | `og.motion.*` | kept | Generated motion for humanoids: the engine's motion model (a 17.6M-parameter student distilled from NVIDIA MotionBricks, og-motion) moves a character between the goals the game gives it, on the GPU. Give an entity with an og.Skeleton (a humanoid rig og.anim.humanoid recognises, or one an og.MotionAgent.rig names) an og.MotionAgent, then queue goals: og.motion.pose (a pose of the model's library where the character stands), og.motion.place (a pose at a place, facing a heading), og.motion.face (turn to a heading), og.motion.walkTo (walk or run to a point) and og.motion.jump (a jump whose arc the simulation owns). og.motion.poses lists the library: idle, walk, run, jump, crouch, wave, cheer. |
| [`destruction`](destruction.md) | `og.destruction.*` | kept | Props that break: walls, crates, pillars, glass. A model cooked with a `fracture { }` block (at the top of a `type model`, or in a glTF's import settings) is cut by the cook into Voronoi chunks bonded where they touch, and the chunks resting on its floor are anchored to the world. Give the entity that draws it (its og.Model) an og.Destructible: hits, og.destruction.damage and og.destruction.explode wear the bonds down, a broken bond splits the prop into islands, an island anchored to the world stays put and every other island falls as one rigid body, and a stress solver (NVIDIA Blast's) breaks what can no longer carry its own weight, so a wall shot out at its foot comes down. |
| [`vfx`](vfx.md) | `og.vfx.*` | kept | Composed effects: one effect (a fireball's impact, a heal, a level-up) as a timeline of elements in an `.ogt` of `type vfx`, Effekseer's and Niagara's systems as text the agent reads and diffs. A file has `duration <seconds>`, `loop true\|false`, `event <seconds> "<name>"` and `impact <seconds>` (`event <seconds> "impact"`, at most one; the same four lines mean the same in a `type vfx2d` pixel effect), and element blocks, each with `at <seconds>` from the effect's start, `offset <x> <y> <z>` and `rotate <x> <y> <z>` (degrees) in the effect's space, `move <x> <y> <z>` (metres per second) and `accelerate <x> <y> <z>` (per second squared) carrying it from its offset from its start (an emitter spawns along the path), and `life <seconds>` or `until <seconds>` for those that last: `emitter "<id>"` (an og.load.emitter asset; `until` stops its emission and its particles live out; `seed`), `mesh sphere \| quad \| ring \| box \| cylinder \| "<model id>"` (drawn with `effect "<id>"`, an effect material: `scale`, a value over its life, `spin` degrees per second, `color`, `blend additive \| alpha`; a `ring` takes its own shape with any of `inner <radius>` (outer 1), `band <0..1>` (its middle row), `height <outer> <inner>` (its edges raised along its axis: a cone, a tube), `arc <start> <length>` (degrees from +x), `segments <n>` and `colors <outer rgba> <band rgba> <inner rgba>`, its u then along the arc and v from the outer edge to the inner, built at load), `trail` (`effect`, `width <head> <tail>`, `lifetime`, `color`, `orbit <radius> <turns per second>` and `rise <metres per second>` about and up the element's y), `beam` (`to <x> <y> <z>` from the element, `width`, `effect`, `segments`, `jitter`, `color`), `light` (a point light: `color`, `intensity` a value over its life, `distance`), `decal` (projected down the element's -y: `uv <u0> <v0> <u1> <v1>`, its region of og.RenderSettings.decalAtlas, `size <x> <y> <z>` with y the depth it reaches, `fade <seconds>` at its end, `color`), `flash` (a soft glow facing the eye: `size` a value over its life, `color`), `shake` (`trauma`, og.camera.shake), `flipbook "<id>"` (a pixel effect, an `.ogt` of `type vfx2d`, or any og.load.flipbook sheet: a camera-facing og.Sprite with og.Flipbook playing its first clip, `size` its height with the width by the frame's shape, `color`, `blend additive \| alpha`, for `life` or its clip's length; its og.FlipbookEvent events, the impact frame among them, reach the game as this effect's og.VfxEvent of the same name) and `sound "<id>"` (`volume`, `pitch <min> <max>` picked by the seed; a child entity with og.AudioSource at the element, cut when the effect despawns). A value is a number, `random <min> <max>` (fixed per instance) or `curve <t> <v> ...` over the element's life. `og cook` checks the file and that what it names is in the project. |

## Guides

Workflow, thresholds and pitfalls no signature states, written by hand beside the IDL (`crates/og-api/guides/`). `og api show <guide>` prints one; `og api find` returns their sections.

| Guide | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`animation`](guide-animation.md) | Motion in an Origin Engine game. Clips and animation graphs, og.motion's generated humanoid motion and why it is presentation only, tweens and timelines, and the timings that make actions read. |
| [`art-review`](guide-art-review.md) | Art judgment for an Origin Engine game. Choosing the style from the premise, requesting every asset through the art brief, the cook's conformance, and reviewing frames and models with measured thresholds. The engine measures; this guide says what is good enough. |
| [`assets`](guide-assets.md) | `og assets` searches the cooked asset inventory for reusable assets, unused outputs, dependencies, and duplicate content. `og cook` writes the inventory to `cooked/.assets.ogt`. The sidecar is not part of a web export. |
| [`components`](guide-components.md) | Every element kind a screen or component document can use, with the props it takes as the document writes them and the states it has. A document uses only what is here: any other kind, property or value is an error that names the form to write. A genre kit's TypeScript members are in the `kits` guide; a style's selectors and tokens in the `screens` guide. |
| [`determinism`](guide-determinism.md) | The engine's rules a game must keep, determinism first, and where they bite: the world and systems, physics, destruction, and lockstep multiplayer over a room. Read before writing simulation code. |
| [`kits`](guide-kits.md) | The genre kits bundled with the engine: what each one draws, how a game installs, changes and reviews one, and how to make a kit of its own. Every kit is TypeScript over the public API and runs unchanged on the web and native hosts. |
| [`looks`](guide-looks.md) | Rendering an Origin Engine game. The look as a preset the game extends, what belongs in the look and what in the scene, lighting and post order, 2D versus 3D, and what a frame costs. |
| [`models`](guide-models.md) | The `type model` asset: a prop or stylised character written as text from the engine's own geometry generators, cooked into the same model blob a glTF becomes. Use it when a model has to follow the look's shape language exactly, or when no catalogue or generated asset fits. |
| [`pixel-vfx`](guide-pixel-vfx.md) | Pixel-art 2D effects (explosions, slashes, spells, portals, beams, auras, sparks, heals, level-ups, weather, loot) as `type vfx2d` files: a Pixel VFX Forge recipe, layered heat fields cut into hard colour bands, that the cook renders into a flipbook sheet with an `impact` event. |
| [`screens`](guide-screens.md) | Screens and HUDs for an Origin Engine game. The UI packs (genre kits and style packs) and how to install and change them, documents versus code, the thresholds for text, contrast and touch, og ui check and preview, and languages with their fonts. |
| [`start`](guide-start.md) | Start here for any Origin Engine game: how a game begins from the empty skeleton and its create block, where the API is answered, the project's shape, and which guide covers what. |
| [`testing`](guide-testing.md) | The build, check and test loop of an Origin Engine game. Invariants first (og.assert, playtest invariants and require), frames only for looks, what an unchecked result means, the probe and dumps, and performance. |
| [`three-to-og`](guide-three-to-og.md) | For an author who knows three.js, or who has a three.js file to bring over. Origin Engine keeps three.js's vocabulary wherever it does not contradict the engine: `Vector3`, position, quaternion and scale, the material parameters, the geometry classes' parameters and defaults, glTF loading, layers. What it does not keep is the object model. A three.js program is a tree of mutable objects that a loop you write renders; an Origin Engine game is a world of entities with plain components, changed by systems on a fixed tick, and the engine draws every frame itself. Read the `start` and `determinism` guides first: this page only maps names. |
| [`ui-materials`](guide-ui-materials.md) | Per-element shader finishes for a game's UI: the foil, holo, burn and rarity presets of the `materials` kit, how to put one on a styled part or an element, how to tune it, and how to write a new one. |

## Units

Field units the docs and Tune use.

| Unit | Means |
|---|---|
| `m` | metres |
| `s` | seconds of simulation time |
| `ms` | milliseconds |
| `rad` | radians |
| `deg` | degrees |
| `hz` | ticks or cycles per second |
| `ticks` | fixed simulation steps |
| `cssPx` | CSS pixels of the play surface, origin at the top left |
| `ratio` | a fraction between 0 and 1 |
| `bytes` | bytes |
| `kg` | kilograms |
| `newton` | newtons: the force that gives a kilogram one metre per second squared |
| `newtonSecond` | newton-seconds: an impulse, the momentum that changes a kilogram's velocity by one metre per second |
| `newtonMetre` | newton-metres: a torque, a newton pushing one metre from the axis it turns about |
| `mps` | metres per second |
| `mps2` | metres per second squared |
| `radps` | radians per second |
| `rpm` | revolutions per minute |
| `perSecond` | a rate per second: the fraction of a value that decays in one second |
| `kgPerM3` | kilograms per cubic metre (per square metre in the 2D profile) |
| `m3` | cubic metres |
| `pascal` | pascals: newtons per square metre, a stress |
| `newtonSecondPerM2` | newton-seconds per square metre: an impulse spread over an area |
| `db` | decibels |
| `evPerSecond` | exposure stops (EV) per second of simulation time |
| `bpm` | beats per minute |
